Dear Requester,

ATISN 26-0141 - Great House Farm, Llandough

Thank you for your request which was received on 29 October.  You asked for:


  1.  You ask that Welsh Government, including Cadw, provides any information it holds about the furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms and other movable property originating from Great House Farm. You ask that this should include inventories, acquisition or transfer records, provenance, photographs and correspondence.
  2.  You state that you have found evidence in a number of historical sources of alternative names by which Great House Farm may have been know in the past, which you have asked us to also search by.  You provide a list of these alternative names for the site in your email of 16:52 on 29 October titled as above, and also in your email of the same time and date titled ‘Nomenclature supplement — Great House Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth’.

I note that you refer to a previous request of 2 July asking for the information listed in point 1 above.  However, this email was only copied to Welsh Government’s Freedom of Information Officer and was not therefore treated as an information request to Welsh Government at that time.

You will receive a response to this latest request by 26 November 2026.  If you have any queries about this request, please do not hesitate to contact me at the address below.  Please remember to quote the reference number above in any future correspondence.

The request you sent me contains personal information about you - for example, your name and address. The Welsh Government will be the data processor for this information and, in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation, it will be processed in order to fulfil our public task and meet our legal obligations under the Act to provide you with a response. We will only use this personal information to deal with your request and any matters which arise as a result of it. We will keep your personal information and all other information relating to your request for three years from the date on which your request is finally closed.  Your personal information will then be disposed of securely.

Under data protection legislation, you have the right:

•              to be informed of the personal data we hold about you and to access it
•              to require us to rectify inaccuracies in that data
•              to (in certain circumstances) object to or restrict processing
•              for (in certain circumstances) your data to be ‘erased’
•              to (in certain circumstances) data portability
•              to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) who is our independent regulator for data protection

Good afternoon, Requester,



Thank you for your enquiry. BGS have made a significant amount of data/records searchable and accessible through the following routes, providing a free, self-service option, to avoid charges that may be incurred if BGS staff were to carry out the searching on your behalf. I hope the following information and links are useful:



  1.  Users can search the Geoindex GeoIndex (onshore) - British Geological Survey<https://www.bgs.ac.uk/map-viewers/geoindex-onshore/> for BGS datasets and navigate the map-based index which holds a wealth of information including boreholes and site investigations that we have collected or have obtained from other sources .I have attached user guidance notes.
  2.  You can search for available mine plans in your area using the Mine Plans Catalogue | OpenGeoscience | Our data | British Geological Survey (BGS)<https://mine-plans.bgs.ac.uk/?_ga=2.8199282.1770190543.1784532596-1462738668.1784532596> .  Many of the plans are scanned and can be freely viewed online. If you identify a BGS plan that cannot be viewed, or you require a pdf copy of a plan you have viewed, please contact [email redacted]<[email redacted]>, providing the BGS mine plan ID and name as we can then check availability and provide a quote to supply.  As a guide, the cost to supply a pdf copy of a plan is £12 + vat per plan or £18 + vat per plan if there isn’t a digital copy available and we have to scan a hard copy.   There is also a minerals data layer on the Geoindex.
  3.  I will direct you to the maps portal BGS maps portal | OpenGeoscience | Our data | British Geological Survey (BGS)<https://webapps.bgs.ac.uk/data/MapsPortal/?_ga=2.39298340.648850980.1793813983-1992634300.1793813983> for free online viewing of over 45,000 BGS geological approved maps and sections. Please let us know of any maps of interest as we can arrange supply (pdf/paper). Your local authority will hold records of land use, registered landfills/ tipping etc. Unapproved historical fieldslip and field notebook records (if available for your site) are held in the BGS strongroom and available to view on request in the BGS Library, by appointment.



Please contact us again if you require further assistance.



Kind regards

Madeleine



Madeleine Stocks
